subject.title: feat(lobster): in-process LLM adapters for embedded runner (#90909)

question: Should the embedded Lobster LLM bridge reuse the existing `llm-task`/OpenClaw policy under a non-shadowing provider id, or intentionally redefine embedded `llm.invoke --provider openclaw` as a new direct in-process contract?
rationale: The choice affects credential exposure, provider/model/auth policy, and compatibility for existing Lobster `openclaw` provider semantics; automation cannot safely choose that product/security boundary.

options.title: Repair before merge
options.body: Use the existing `llm-task` policy or a shared equivalent, prevent host credentials from reaching command env, choose a non-shadowing provider id unless maintainers approve otherwise, and require live proof.

options.title: Accept the new direct contract
options.body: Keep the embedded `openclaw` direct adapter but document the intentional routing and policy differences before merge.

options.title: Pause behind the design issue
options.body: Keep this PR open as a candidate while the canonical issue settles provider naming and security policy.

recommendation.title: Repair before merge
recommendation.body: Use the existing `llm-task` policy or a shared equivalent, prevent host credentials from reaching command env, choose a non-shadowing provider id unless maintainers approve otherwise, and require live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across both Lobster runtime maintenance and llm-task/provider policy.
